title: Money, shared
hook: Zacchaeus climbs a sycamore, Jesus invites himself to dinner, and the rich man names a share: generosity as an answer to welcome

segments.voice: A paycheck lands, and the first thought is the bills. Now Jericho. A crowd packs the road because Jesus is passing through, and Zacchaeus wants to see him. He's the chief of the tax collectors, and he's rich. He's also short, and he can't see over the crowd. So he runs ahead and climbs a sycamore tree. Jesus reaches the tree, stops, and looks up.
screen: `A PAYCHECK, AND THE BILLS.` → `A CROWD IN JERICHO.` → `A SHORT RICH MAN IN A TREE.` → `JESUS LOOKS UP.`

segments.voice: Here's what Luke says he said: "Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house." The crowd grumbles: he's gone to be the guest of a sinner. Then Zacchaeus stands up: "Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold." And Jesus answers: this day is salvation come to this house. Notice the order. Jesus doesn't demand the money first. He invites himself to dinner. The giving comes after the welcome, as an answer to it. Many Christians read the story this way: generosity is a response to grace, not a price paid for it. And Zacchaeus doesn't give everything. He names a share, out loud, and he makes things right with anyone he cheated. Some churches teach a regular share called a tithe, a tenth, drawn from the Hebrew Bible; others leave the amount to each person. Either way, wealth used well, in Luke's story, is neither hoarded nor thrown off in guilt. It's a share, named, after you've been welcomed.

segments.voice: Count on your fingers what you've been given this month: a meal, a kindness, a paycheck, a ride. Go slowly, one finger at a time. When you run out, name one share you could give from it, however small, and to whom.
Money: in the Zacchaeus story, wealth answered with a share, named out loud, after being welcomed first.
Your line: a share. Zacchaeus named his after Jesus came to dinner. See you tomorrow.
